sections.h2: Which Grayson County offices deal with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Grayson's sheriff takes the money, and the PVA sets the value. The sheriff works from 117 S. Main Street in Leitchfield, KY 42754, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Central Time, phone (270) 259-3024. For assessed values and exemption papers the sheriff's FAQ points callers to the PVA at (270) 259-4838.

A third office enters once a real property bill is transferred. The Grayson County Clerk, at (270) 259-5295, quotes payoffs on those older bills. A buyer's title company will want to know which of the three offices holds each year, so keep the numbers handy before listing.

  • Current bills can be paid on the sheriff's online portal, by mail or at the counter. Cards are accepted in both places, with a processing fee.
  • Only the full bill is taken. No installments, no partial payments.
  • No bill by November 10? Call the sheriff for a copy and give the property address and owner name.
  • With an escrow account, hand the bill to your lender and confirm later that the payment went out.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Grayson County itself?
sections.html:
Rural west central Kentucky describes most of Grayson County, with Leitchfield serving as seat and largest city. Settlers got a county of their own in 1810, cut from Hardin and Ohio, and it now spans roughly 497 square miles of land. Caneyville and Clarkson are the other two cities, and Big Clifty is a census-designated place.

Two Army Corps of Engineers lakes shape the local market. Rough River Lake lies along the northern border and Nolin River Lake along the southeast edge, which is why businesses use the label "Twin Lakes." The Western Kentucky Parkway and US 62 carry most traffic, and the county runs its own airport. The 2020 census counted 13,275 housing units here, 21.4 percent of them vacant.

Fire has shaped the county seat's story: three courthouses burned, in 1864, 1896 and 1936. The county sits in Kentucky's Western Coal Field region, though only its western third holds coal, and it borders six counties: Breckinridge, Hardin, Hart, Edmonson, Butler and Ohio. Leitchfield voted to allow alcohol sales in 2016 after limited sales began in 2010.

The Census Bureau's county table for Grayson gives this picture:

  • Population: 27,406 in July 2025, a 3.7 percent rise since April 2020.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 74.6 percent, across 10,129 households.
  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $164,600.
  • Median owner costs: $1,274 a month with a mortgage, $416 without. Persons per household: 2.58.
  • Median gross rent: $658. Median household income: $50,757. Persons in poverty: 22.4 percent.

Someone dealing with a roof leak, a cracked foundation or a lien can sell a Grayson County house as-is to a cash buyer.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Grayson County payment windows?
sections.html:
The sheriff's 2026 schedule opens the discount on November 1 and closes it on November 30. Face amount is due all of December, and 2027 brings the penalties. Kentucky's own default under KRS 134.015 is a discount through November 1, so follow the sheriff's published windows.

sections.h2: What are fire and rescue dues on a Grayson County bill?
sections.html:
Many bills here carry a fire and rescue membership charge for the county's fire districts. An owner can drop it for one year by signing an opt-out form and sending the form in with the payment. The sheriff asks owners to call before paying online if they plan to opt out.

The form carries a warning for anyone who sells or leaves a house empty. Under KRS 75.450, an owner who opts out can be billed by the fire district for at least $500 or $1,000, depending on the type of facility, after a fire or other non-medical incident at the property. A new form is needed every year.

If you are listing, settle the dues question before paying the bill and tell the closing agent which way you went.

sections.h2: How can a Grayson County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the Grayson County PVA first, since Kentucky closes the appeal door to owners who skip it. Call (270) 259-4838. Roll inspection lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May.

  • Expect the PVA to walk through how the number was built and to write down your claimed value and any agreed change.
  • No later than the next business day after inspection ends, take the appeal to the county clerk.
  • A local board hears cases roughly four to five weeks later. Come with repair estimates, insurance records, photos and nearby sale listings, because an appeal with no paper behind it is denied.
  • Missing the hearing forfeits the later route to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

A paid representative must come from the state's approved professions, such as attorneys, CPAs and appraisers, and needs your written authority. When bills were printed before the case ended and the board lands above your claim, the clerk sends a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Can Grayson County owners get a homestead break?
sections.html:
Grayson County owners aged 65 or up, or totally disabled, can claim the break on the house where they live. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the state sets it at $49,100 off assessed value. At Grayson's Census median of $164,600, taxable value would fall to $115,500.

Take proof of age (birth certificate, license or passport) to the PVA. For a disability claim, ask the PVA which papers prove the classification and how often to renew.

After a sale, ask the PVA what to file so the break comes off the house you sold and can be claimed at your next home.

sections.h2: Who pays Grayson County back taxes when a house sells?
sections.html:
The parcel keeps the debt, so a buyer's title search will turn it up. Taxes are the owner's debt from January 1, and the lien on an unpaid bill can last 11 years whoever owns the house, per KRS 134.420.

At the clerk, interest accrues at 1 percent per month and commissions are layered on. The county attorney mails notices at the 30-day and 60-day marks. The clerk can hold a sale of the certificates 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer at that sale may tack on charges of its own.

Get two payoff figures before listing: the current year from the sheriff and any transferred bills from the clerk. Both can be settled at the closing table from what the buyer pays.

faqs.q: When does the 2026 discount end in Grayson County?
faqs.a: On November 30, 2026. The sheriff's schedule starts the discount November 1, then shows face amount for December and a 5 percent penalty in January 2027.

faqs.q: Does the Grayson County Sheriff accept installments?
faqs.a: No. The office wants the whole bill at once and refuses partial payments. If a lender escrows your taxes, it can send the full amount for you.

faqs.q: My Grayson County bill never came. What now?
faqs.a: Phone the sheriff at (270) 259-3024 after November 10 and ask for a duplicate. Give the property address and the owner's name.

faqs.q: Where do I settle a Grayson County bill after April 15?
faqs.a: With the County Clerk at (270) 259-5295. Real property bills still open on that date move to the clerk, who quotes the payoff including interest and commissions.

faqs.q: Who takes homestead applications in Grayson County?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (270) 259-4838. Bring proof of age or disability. The 2025 and 2026 exemption takes $49,100 off assessed value.
